report:
PASS for the corrected manuscript’s stated partial theorem. This does not establish the unchanged original P14.4 target or close any other original atom. I found no material mathematical defect or essential unresolved dependency in the partial result. One harmless normalization clarification is recorded below.

I treated the complete B body as the sole mathematical grant, within the task’s exact actual-big rational-bundle domain. Its internal G0/G1 statements were not used as separate grants. Historical acceptance claims, compilation, hashes and author-reading ledgers supplied no mathematical evidence. The task-grant passage below is deliberately unnumbered because B is excluded from the external-premise registry.

I independently opened the literal BEGZ v2 and DDL v3 primary sources. The pertinent complete units checked were BEGZ §1.2 through Proposition 1.6, including its local finite-mass criterion, and DDL Theorems 2.3/2.4, the §3.2 membership argument, and Theorem 3.12 with its preceding in-paper supporting arguments. The manuscript invokes published analytic results; it does not present their bibliography as a self-contained reconstruction. Their precise imported claims are registered below. [BEGZ v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0812.3674v2), [DDL v3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1705.05796v3).

The curve construction is sound. The specified ddᶜ convention gives unit Fubini–Study mass and ddᶜG(·,t)=δ_t−ω. The elementary inequality establishing G≤0 is correct. Uniform local logarithmic L¹ bounds justify Fubini and the distributional Hessian identity. Fatou gives upper semicontinuity, and integration of the logarithmic submean inequalities gives the canonical quasi-psh representative. Compact support makes the potential smooth away from its support, including near infinity. Admissibility supplies exactly the prescribed poles; the resulting local subharmonic primitives also establish polarity and area zero. Supports of finite positive sums are their unions, so the nonpositive kernel proves closure under those sums and positive scaling.

Exponential integrability is established without an unstated Lelong-number theorem. Atomlessness permits a neighborhood mass δ with hδ<1. Jensen reduces the exponential to an average of |z−t|^(−2hδ); its planar integral is uniformly finite. The complementary potential is bounded on the smaller neighborhood. Truncation and Fubini justify this argument even at the infinite values of the potential.

The holomorphic-pullback lemma also holds at critical points. Nonconstancy and the identity theorem give a finite-order Taylor term at every relevant point. A suitable complex line has order d. Shrinking the disc isolates its d zeros; nearby parameters retain that number and keep all roots in the smaller disc. Factoring these roots leaves a zero-free unit. Boundary bounds and the maximum principle bound its reciprocal uniformly. Hölder then yields uniform integrability of |f−t|^(−2ε) when dε<1. Choosing δ<1/(hd) completes the Jensen argument. Boundary upper bounds likewise control the unit’s logarithm, establishing the logarithmic L¹ estimate needed later. Holomorphic choices of individual roots are unnecessary. Local psh primitives give the canonical pullback and define the positive polar current, rather than assuming a distributional pullback exists.

The geometric cone and its order are correctly stated. The conditions a,b,c≥0 and m≤b make every term of T_D positive. Addition and scaling preserve admissibility and the mass constraint. Constants act on the reconstructed primitive. On a fixed coefficient leaf, cancellation of the finite common exceptional term off E, together with the existence of points off E over every curve point, proves both directions of the kernel-test order. The conventions at a=0 and zero scaling avoid undefined products with −∞.

The bigness and non-nefness proofs are valid. The three hyperplanes through the Segre image of p generate its ideal on Y. Their graph realizes the blowup as a closed subvariety of Y×P², so 2(H_z+H_w)−E is ample. Formula (3.5) consequently supplies a Kähler current for every a,b,c>0. The intersections H_zE=H_wE=0 and E²=−1 give α_DE=−a, excluding nefness. Integrating the geometric current in the w direction near the finite support recovers (b−m)ω_z+ν. Its area-singular part is precisely ν. Thus current reconstruction does recover the measure, while correctly leaving the additive constant undetermined.

Compatibility holds for every given smooth proper bimeromorphic modification in the stated theorem. Both fibrations remain nonconstant. The pulled section defines the full total divisor p*E with all multiplicities, and the pullback-integrability lemma constructs the polar term. Composition of primitives, sections and smooth forms proves compatibility under subsequent modifications. The carrier map follows directly from extension of coherent ideals: sums, products, units and supports behave as stated, and the Cartier-divisor ideal identity is exact. No topology identification is needed. Smooth reference changes preserve multiplier ideals; the competitor bijection proves the rooftop covariance formula. Transporting the obstacle is essential, and the manuscript correctly distinguishes this from resetting it to zero.

All real-scale multiplier-ideal formulas check out. Near E the polar term is smooth, so radial integration requires j+1>ta and gives exactly j≥⌊ta⌋, including integral ta. Expansion in the normal coordinate proves necessity for arbitrary germs. Elsewhere, exponential integrability gives the unit ideal. On a modification, the polar term is smooth near the total exceptional divisor and has integrable exponentials everywhere else. This proves (5.2) without any normal-crossing assumption. Separate radial integrals justify the componentwise floor formula only in the asserted SNC case. At supported semivaluations, the divisor ideal has infinite value once its exponent becomes positive; at finite values the elementary floor limit applies. Consequently the asymptotic shadow formula is valid on the entire specified point set, without divisorial density or 0·∞ arithmetic. Its operation laws concern asymptotic profiles, not an incorrect additive floor identity.

The first and top nonpluripolar products, their local finiteness and their raw masses are established in the claimed domains. On W, the actual primitive has the closed locally complete pluripolar pole set p⁻¹E∪(q∘p)⁻¹S. Its current equals p*S_D on the complement. That complement product has locally finite mass because it is smooth. The exceptional divisor has ambient volume zero. Away from the critical locus, submersion coordinates and Fubini show that the inverse image of S has ambient volume zero. The critical locus lies locally in the zero set of a nonzero holomorphic derivative and also has volume zero. Thus neither smooth product has coefficient mass on the removed set. The local truncation construction therefore gives exactly (p*S_D)^k for k=1,2. This argument needs no Kähler assertion about W. The two curve pullback forms have square zero, leaving 2c(b−m) times the pulled product volume. Change of variables on the bimeromorphic isomorphism loci gives integral one, hence the stated unchanged raw mass. The case m=b legitimately gives zero mass; no probability normalization is attempted.

The corrected approximation proposition is sound. For a fixed state, multiplication of ν by 1−1/j preserves admissibility and produces decreasing primitives, including at poles. Products and masses converge by their explicit polynomial formulas, rather than by an unsupported general Monge–Ampère continuity assertion. For the generalized estimate, common compact affine support is sufficient: the finite-root argument and a finite chart cover bound the composed logarithmic kernel’s L¹ norm uniformly in its parameter on each fixed compact region of each fixed modification. Integration against the total-variation measure gives the kernel-TV term. The pulled divisor logarithm is locally integrable. The triangle inequality therefore gives exactly the three displayed error terms for a, ν and κ. The coefficients b,c affect the smooth background but not this primitive formula. Differences are legitimate almost everywhere; the pole sets have ambient volume zero. Constants may depend on the fixed modification, as permitted. No closure under arbitrary weak measure limits is asserted.

The oscillating-constant counterexample satisfies its stated same-class domain. The states (1,1,1,0,κ_j) are admissible and lie in one big non-nef class. On a positive-volume compact region off E, consecutive primitives differ by the constant one. They are not L¹-Cauchy, although their measures agree. This establishes the need to control the primitive coordinates. Envelope homogeneity, constant invariance and monotonicity follow from competitor scaling, reindexing and inclusion; current and top-mass scaling have the stated factors.

The Cantor measures are independently constructed. Disjoint nested children and lengths tending to zero define the Bernoulli pushforward probability with cylinder masses 2^(−j). Those masses prove atomlessness and identify its support. At each support point, restricting the kernel integral to its level-j interval gives −2·2^j, while the remaining contribution is nonpositive. Hence the potential is −∞ throughout the support. Translation gives the second admissible probability with disjoint support. No capacity formula or earlier Cantor-family verdict is needed.

The strengthened mandatory example is valid. On every specified modification the two complete real-scale ideal families agree by (5.2), and both first and second nonpluripolar currents agree because the measure masses are equal. Their common top mass is 2c(b−s)>0. The maximum of the two curve potentials is bounded because each support has a neighborhood on which the other potential is smooth, and both are smooth on the remaining compact set. The maximum primitive consequently differs from ae by a bounded amount and has mass 2bc. Under the explicit hypothetical common-envelope assumption, that envelope dominates the maximum but has mass 2c(b−s). Applying mass monotonicity gives the stated contradiction. The antecedent is used only to derive this contradiction; it is not presumed established. The compact Kähler, big-class, canonical-psh and positive-mass hypotheses are all satisfied. Neither zero-mass maximality nor commutation of envelopes with maxima is used. Envelope separation is asserted on X; the tower statement concerns ideal/product/mass equality. The numerical specialization has mass one, the stated first and top products, and ordinary self-intersection 7/4.

The application of B stays within its grant. For positive rational a,b,c, X is a smooth integral projective surface over trivially valued C and L is an actual big rational bundle. Negative restriction degree on E forces every cleared-degree section to contain σ_E^(ℓa). After division, normal birational section descent gives the entire generated pullback system from Y. Thus the stationary moving pair is genuinely A=π*O(b,c), T=aE. Its section dimensions also give vol(L)=A²=2bc. For nearby defining bundles, repeated negative-degree restriction forces vanishing at least −c₁(B_i)·E; rounding only strengthens this lower bound. Those coefficients tend to a, and the incoming generic constants tend to zero. B’s order determination therefore bounds every normalized endpoint by q_T. The zero-weight complete system realizes q_T, proving that it is the granted reference. The product moving model has C³=3dA², zero auxiliary energy and its sole central component contributes 2bcδ_v₀. B’s complete-system identification consequently supplies this reference operator. The horizontal factor aE is retained. These are genuine operator calculations in B’s domain, not a relatively nef model representing the non-nef generic L. No complex-to-NA measure map is supplied or inferred.

The asserted information-loss boundaries are supported. Comparing ν=0 with a positive admissible ν shows that raw mass does not descend to the identical ideal shadow. The two disjoint-support measures show that even the specified entire ideal/product/mass tower does not determine the normalized P-envelope. The bounded nonconstant maximum cannot be another admissible kernel potential: a nonzero admissible measure gives poles, while the zero measure gives a constant. A harmless normalization clarification is appropriate in the final maximum paragraph: the winner has Hessian −ω for U_{μ_i}, and −sω for the actual scaled weights U_{sμ_i}. Both prove nonconstancy, so this requires no substantial repair.

The established scope is the explicit geometric measure sector on this projective blown-up surface, with its declared fibration, kernel, metric, references and additional complex measure datum. Its real coefficients remain algebraic Néron–Severi directions. It does not establish an intrinsic full NA cone, arbitrary P-type realization, closure under maxima, PL approximation, a DXZ/MP projection, common-scope operator comparison, or an energy theory. The full big non-nef transcendental and nonprojective requirements remain unestablished here. P14.4 and the other original atoms retain their unchanged completion criteria.

passages.statement: BEGZ, arXiv:0812.3674v2, §1.2, Definitions 1.1–1.2 and Propositions 1.4/1.6: For local psh u₁,…,uₚ on a complex n-manifold, 1≤p≤n, the nonpluripolar product is determined by 1_{∩{uⱼ>−N}}⋀ⱼddᶜmax(uⱼ,−N), provided these currents have uniformly bounded local masses. When defined, it is positive, depends only on the currents, is plurifine-local and charges no pluripolar set. If the potentials are locally bounded outside a closed locally complete pluripolar Z, existence is equivalent to local finiteness near Z of the complement’s Bedford–Taylor product; the result is its trivial extension. Products of closed positive (1,1)-currents on compact Kähler manifolds always exist.
passages.quote: putting no mass on pluripolar subsets
